page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and SHA-NI. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is minimal at 1 GB of network-attached storage, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top tier. Text processing via Geekbench also ranks in the top tier. However, multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation, falls into the average tier. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with cached small-block reads reaching 879.9 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 72.42 GB/sec. For machine learning, text generation using a small 135M parameter model is highly efficient, whereas prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak, placing in the bottom quarter of tested systems.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high memory density, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The primary tradeoff is the lack of substantial local storage, meaning applications must rely on network-attached storage for data persistence, which may introduce latency. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.
